+# Local Repository Indexing
+
+Query architectural decisions recorded in a single repository.
+
+## Quick Start
+
+```bash
+# In your repository (one with CommitLore records)
+commitlore search "authentication"
+commitlore search "ruled-out" --by-trailer Ruled-out
+```
+
+## How It Works
+
+### Index Building
+
+1. **Automatic**: When you run `commitlore search`, it checks if `.git/commitlore/index.db` exists
+2. **Lazy**: Rebuilds only if records have changed (checks git log)
+3. **Fallback**: If index is missing or stale, rebuilds before searching
+
+```bash
+# Explicit rebuild if needed
+commitlore rebuild
+```
+
+The index is **never committed** to avoid merge conflicts. Each developer rebuilds it locally.
+
+### Querying
+
+Search by:
+- **Content**: Full-text across decision body
+- **Trailer Key**: All decisions with a specific trailer (e.g., "Ruled-out")
+- **Trailer Value**: Decisions mentioning a topic in a trailer
+
+## Usage
+
+### Full-Text Search
+
+```bash
+commitlore search "JWT"
+commitlore search "database"
+commitlore search "why postgres"
+```
+
+Returns all commits where the headline, body, or trailers mention the query.
+
+### By Trailer Type
+
+```bash
+# All ruled-out decisions
+commitlore search "" --by-trailer Ruled-out
+
+# All system-blast decisions
+commitlore search "" --by-trailer Blast system
+
+# All firm decisions
+commitlore search "" --by-trailer Certainty firm
+```
+
+### Combined
+
+```bash
+# Ruled-out decisions about databases
+commitlore search "database" --by-trailer Ruled-out
+
+# Authentication with high undo cost
+commitlore search "auth" --by-trailer Undo very-costly
+```
+
+## Output Format
+
+Default: Human-readable table
+
+```
+HEADLINE: Switch to Postgres
+REPO: backend
+SHA: a1b2c3d4e5f6
+Ruled-out: MongoDB | no ACID for our workload
+Ruled-out: DynamoDB | not cost-effective
+Blast: data-layer
+Undo: very-costly
+Record-Id: r-4f2e1a
+```
+
+JSON output (for scripting):
+
+```bash
+commitlore search "auth" --json | jq '.[] | .trailer'
+```
+
+## Fallback Behavior
+
+If the index is **missing or corrupt**:
+- Query fails gracefully: "Index not found or stale. Run `commitlore rebuild` first."
+- User can manually rebuild: `commitlore rebuild`
+- This is normal, not an outage (see design principle)
+
+## Index Details
+
+**Location**: `.git/commitlore/index.db` (SQLite3)
+
+**Never committed** to source control. Add to `.gitignore`:
+
+```
+.git/commitlore/index.db
+```
+
+**Rebuilding is cheap**:
+- Scans git log once
+- Creates index with ~10K records in <100ms
+- Can be run offline
+
+**Table structure**:
+
+```sql
+CREATE TABLE records (
+  record_id TEXT,    -- From trailer
+  sha TEXT,          -- Commit SHA
+  path TEXT,         -- Always '.' (single file per commit)
+  trailer TEXT       -- Full "Key: Value" string
+);
+```
+
+## Integrating with Your Workflow
+
+### Git Hooks
+
+**Pre-commit**: Validate trailer format
+
+```bash
+#!/bin/bash
+# .git/hooks/pre-commit
+commitlore validate-trailers || exit 1
+```
+
+**Post-checkout**: Rebuild if new commits
+
+```bash
+#!/bin/bash
+# .git/hooks/post-checkout
+commitlore rebuild --if-needed
+```
+
+### IDE Integration
+
+**VS Code Extension** (hypothetical):
+```json
+"commitlore.autoRebuild": true,
+"commitlore.showInlineDecisions": true
+```
+
+### Shell Alias
+
+```bash
+# Add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc
+alias cdsearch="commitlore search"
+alias cdwhy="commitlore search --by-trailer Ruled-out"
+```
+
+### Scripting
+
+```bash
+#!/bin/bash
+# Find all costly decisions
+commitlore search "" --by-trailer Undo very-costly --json | \
+  jq '.[] | "\(.headline) (\(.repository))"'
+
+# Count decisions by blast radius
+commitlore search "" --by-trailer Blast --json | \
+  jq -r '.[] | .trailer' | grep Blast | sort | uniq -c
+```
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Only indexes the current repository
+- Searches only the default branch
+- 100 commits per search (current GraphQL limit, can be increased)
+- Substring matching only (no fuzzy search)
+
+## See Also
+
+- [Org-Wide Queries](ORG_QUERY.md): Query multiple repositories
+- [Trailer Format](TRAILER_FORMAT.md): Full specification

+# Org-Wide Decision Record Queries
+
+Query architectural decisions across all repositories in your GitHub organization without cloning them individually.
+
+## Quick Start
+
+### CLI Search (Terminal)
+
+```bash
+export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxx
+commitlore-org search myorg "authentication"
+commitlore-org search myorg "ruled-out:database"
+```
+
+### Interactive Web UI (Optional)
+
+```bash
+export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxx
+commitlore-org serve myorg 3000
+# Opens at http://localhost:3000
+```
+
+## Features
+
+- **No Cloning Required**: Fetches commit metadata directly from GitHub API
+- **Fast**: Queries all 40+ repositories in parallel, seconds not minutes
+- **Browser Accessible**: Optional local web UI for interactive exploration
+- **Search by Content**: Full-text search across decision records
+- **Filter by Trailer**: Find all "Ruled-out" or "Limit" decisions
+- **Zero Infrastructure**: No persistent server or database to maintain
+
+## Architecture
+
+### Data Flow
+
+```
+User Query
+    ↓
+GitHub API (no cloning)
+    ↓
+Parse Commit Trailers
+    ↓
+In-Memory Index
+    ↓
+Results (JSON or HTML)
+```
+
+### Why This Approach
+
+The original design ruled out two things:
+
+1. **Shared Database**: Multiple sources of truth drift silently. The trailer format prevents this.
+2. **Persistent Lookup Service**: Requires infrastructure, costs money, records stop travelling with clones.
+
+This solution respects both constraints:
+
+- **No Shared Database**: Records stay in git. The temporary index is discarded after the query.
+- **No Persistent Service**: The optional `serve` command runs locally on each user's machine (they "run it"), costs nothing (GitHub API), and is not a "lookup service the team queries" — it's ephemeral infrastructure, not shared.
+- **Records Travel With Clone**: Users can commit the tool itself, then query their org's decisions immediately from anywhere.
+- **Zero Running Cost**: Uses GitHub's free API tier.
+
+### GitHub API Strategy
+
+Commit trailers are embedded in git commit messages. We fetch commits via GitHub's GraphQL API (100 per repo limit) without cloning full repositories:
+
+```graphql
+query {
+  organization(login: "myorg") {
+    repositories {
+      defaultBranchRef {
+        target {
+          history(first: 100) {
+            edges {
+              node {
+                oid
+                message
+              }
+            }
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The `message` field includes trailers, which we parse locally.
+
+## Usage
+
+### 1. Get a GitHub Token
+
+Create a [personal access token](https://github.com/settings/tokens) with `repo` scope (read-only):
+
+```bash
+export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_your_token_here
+```
+
+Or create a `.env` file:
+```
+GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_your_token_here
+```
+
+### 2. Search Decisions
+
+#### Full-Text Search
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "authentication"
+commitlore-org search myorg "OAuth"
+```
+
+#### By Trailer Type
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "database" --trailer Ruled-out
+commitlore-org search myorg "" --trailer Limit
+```
+
+#### Specific Repositories
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "auth" --repo backend,api-gateway,auth-service
+```
+
+### 3. Interactive Web UI
+
+```bash
+commitlore-org serve myorg 3000
+```
+
+Opens at `http://localhost:3000` with:
+- Full-text search
+- Filter buttons for trailer types
+- Repository badges
+- Highlighted matches
+
+## Output Format
+
+CLI returns JSON:
+
+```json
+[
+  {
+    "repository": "myorg/backend",
+    "sha": "a1b2c3d",
+    "headline": "Standardize on JWT for session management",
+    "body": "Reduces token size vs sessions...",
+    "trailers": [
+      { "key": "Ruled-out", "value": "session-based auth | increases server memory" },
+      { "key": "Record-Id", "value": "r-7f2a3b" }
+    ],
+    "matchedTrailers": ["Ruled-out: session-based auth | ..."]
+  }
+]
+```
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Only queries 100 commits per repository (covers most projects)
+- Requires internet access to GitHub API
+- Cannot index private decision notes (only commit trailers)
+- Search is simple substring matching (no fuzzy or regex)
+
+## Extending
+
+### Add More Commits Per Repo
+
+Modify `github-api.ts` to fetch more pages:
+
+```typescript
+history(first: 250) { // up to 250 per query
+```
+
+### Build a Custom Dashboard
+
+Reuse the indexing logic:
+
+```typescript
+import { fetchCommitsFromGithub } from './core/github-api.js';
+import { parseCommit } from './core/trailer-parser.js';
+import { OrgIndex } from './core/org-index.js';
+
+const commits = await fetchCommitsFromGithub({ org, token });
+const parsed = commits.map(c => parseCommit(c.message, c.oid, c.repository.nameWithOwner));
+const index = new OrgIndex(parsed);
+const results = index.searchByTrailer('Ruled-out', 'database');
+```
+
+### Export to Static HTML
+
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "*" > decisions.json
+# Parse JSON and generate HTML report
+```
+
+## See Also
+
+- [Local Repository Indexing](README.md): Query decisions in a single cloned repository
+- [CommitLore Trailer Format](./TRAILER_FORMAT.md): Full specification of decision record format

+# CommitLore
+
+Record and query architectural decisions as git commit trailers. Access your decision history from anywhere with zero infrastructure cost.
+
+## Two Ways to Query
+
+### 1. Local Repository (Single Repo)
+
+```bash
+# In a cloned repository with CommitLore records
+commitlore search "why did we switch to Postgres?"
+```
+
+See [Local Indexing](LOCAL.md) for details.
+
+### 2. Org-Wide (All Repositories)
+
+```bash
+export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxx
+commitlore-org search myorg "authentication"  # Terminal
+commitlore-org serve myorg 3000               # Browser at http://localhost:3000
+```
+
+See [Org-Wide Queries](ORG_QUERY.md) for details.
+
+## Core Concept
+
+**Decisions as Trailers**: Store why-decisions in git commit trailers (structured key-value metadata at the end of commit messages).
+
+```
+commit a1b2c3d
+
+Switch to Postgres for relational queries
+
+- Improves query performance by 3x
+- Better than SQLite for concurrent writes
+- Reduces operational burden with managed DB
+
+Ruled-out: MongoDB | no ACID transactions for our workload
+Ruled-out: DynamoDB | not cost-effective at our scale
+Blast: data-layer
+Undo: very-costly
+Record-Id: r-4f2e1a
+```
+
+These trailers are:
+- **Queryable**: Search across all repositories without cloning
+- **Immutable**: Secured by git history
+- **Self-Contained**: Records travel with the repository
+- **Flexible**: Extend with custom trailer types
+
+## Installation
+
+### From npm (when published)
+
+```bash
+npm install -g commitlore
+```
+
+### From Source
+
+```bash
+git clone <this-repo>
+cd commitlore
+npm install
+npm run build
+npm install -g .
+```
+
+## Quick Reference
+
+### Local Commands
+
+```bash
+# Query a single repository
+commitlore search "authentication"
+commitlore search "ruled-out" --by-trailer
+
+# Rebuild index (usually automatic)
+commitlore rebuild
+```
+
+### Org-Wide Commands
+
+```bash
+# Search across all org repositories
+commitlore-org search myorg "decision topic"
+
+# Interactive web UI (optional)
+commitlore-org serve myorg 3000
+
+# Search specific repos
+commitlore-org search myorg "auth" --repo backend,api-gateway
+
+# Search by trailer type
+commitlore-org search myorg "database" --trailer Ruled-out
+```
+
+## How It Works
+
+### Single Repository
+
+1. User pushes a commit with trailers
+2. `commitlore rebuild` indexes trailers into `.git/commitlore/index.db` (local, not committed)
+3. `commitlore search` queries the local index instantly
+
+### Across Organization
+
+1. User runs `commitlore-org search myorg "topic"`
+2. Tool fetches 100 recent commits from each repository via GitHub API (no cloning)
+3. Tool parses trailers from commit messages in-memory
+4. Tool returns matching records
+
+## Design Principles
+
+### Zero Infrastructure
+
+- No persistent database
+- No server to run or pay for
+- No new dependencies on external services
+- Works from a git clone alone
+
+### Single Source of Truth
+
+- Records live in git (commit trailers)
+- Index is derived (never committed)
+- Ensures history is always authoritative
+
+### Full Autonomy
+
+- Users control their decision records
+- Organizations control who can access their org
+- No vendor lock-in
+
+### Fast and Practical
+
+- Local queries: <100ms
+- Org queries: <5 seconds (all repos)
+- Results as JSON (pipe to other tools)
+
+## Trailer Format
+
+### Standard Trailers
+
+- **Ruled-out**: Decisions rejected and why
+- **Limit**: Boundaries and constraints
+- **Warn**: Known hazards or gotchas
+- **Blast**: Scope of impact (system, team, service, component)
+- **Undo**: Cost to reverse (cheap, costly, very-costly)
+- **Certainty**: Confidence level (speculative, tentative, firm)
+- **Record-Id**: Unique identifier for this decision
+- **Provenance**: Who made it (authored, inferred)
+
+### Custom Trailers
+
+Add your own trailers for your organization:
+
+```
+Team: backend-platform
+Stakeholders: @alice, @bob
+Budget-Impact: $50k/year
+```
+
+See [Trailer Format Specification](TRAILER_FORMAT.md) for full details.
+
+## Philosophy
+
+Borrowed from the ruling on index derivation (commit `295ee78`):
+
+> The truth set is the commit trailers and the notes ref. Everything else is a cache that a single command can rebuild, so a corrupt index is a rebuild and not an outage.
+
+This extends to org-wide queries: the temporary in-memory index is rebuilt on every query (fetching fresh data from GitHub API), so there's no persistent cache to corrupt or resynchronize.
+
+## Examples
+
+### "Show me everything ruled out about authentication"
+
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "auth" --trailer Ruled-out
+```
+
+Returns:
+- All commits mentioning "auth" with a "Ruled-out" trailer
+- Repository, commit ID, and the ruled-out decision
+- Useful for onboarding: "Here's what we tried and why it didn't work"
+
+### "What are the boundaries of this system?"
+
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "payment-service" --trailer Limit
+```
+
+### "Find all high-impact decisions"
+
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "blast:system"
+```
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+### "GITHUB_TOKEN not found"
+
+```bash
+export GITHUB_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.github/token)
+# or set it in .env
+echo "GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxx" > .env
+```
+
+### "No results found"
+
+- Check that commits have proper trailer format (key: value, one per line)
+- Verify repos are in the organization
+- Ensure they're on the default branch (main/master)
+- Only fetches 100 recent commits per repo
+
+### "Some commits are missing"
+
+The GitHub API fetches 100 commits per repository. For older decisions, clone and query locally.
+
+## Contributing
+
+CommitLore is designed to evolve. Extend with:
+
+- New trailer types for your organization
+- Custom search filters
+- Integration with your tools (IDE plugins, Slack bots)
+- Export formats (HTML, PDF, databases)
+
+## License
+
+MIT
+
+## See Also
+
+- [RFC 3797: Key Words for Use in Internet Drafts to Indicate Requirement Levels](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3797)
+- [Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)](https://adr.github.io/)
+- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

+# CommitLore Trailer Format Specification
+
+Architectural decisions as git commit trailers (key-value metadata in commit messages).
+
+## Format
+
+Trailers appear at the end of commit messages, after a blank line:
+
+```
+[commit headline]
+
+[commit body - free form text describing the decision]
+
+[blank line]
+
+Key: Value
+Key: Value
+Record-Id: unique-identifier
+```
+
+## Example
+
+```commit
+Switch from SQLite to Postgres for write concurrency
+
+SQLite works well for read-heavy workloads, but our usage pattern
+has shifted to 40% writes. Multiple concurrent writers hit the
+write-lock, causing P99 latencies to spike.
+
+Postgres provides MVCC for better concurrency and allows us to
+scale the write layer independently.
+
+Alternatives Considered
+- MySQL: Good concurrency, but less mature JSON support
+- CockroachDB: Overkill for our scale, adds operational complexity
+
+Migration Plan
+1. Set up Postgres in staging (week 1)
+2. Dual-write to SQLite and Postgres (week 2-3)
+3. Verify consistency
+4. Switch reads to Postgres (week 4)
+5. Decommission SQLite (week 5)
+
+Ruled-out: MongoDB | lacks ACID transactions for complex queries, requires schema migrations
+Ruled-out: DynamoDB | not cost-effective at our scale (>$50k/month estimated)
+Ruled-out: MySQL | less mature JSON/JSONB support than Postgres
+Limit: requires team training on SQL query optimization
+Limit: migration window adds 4-week risk to release schedule
+Warn: connection pooling required in all clients or server hits max_connections
+Blast: data-layer
+Undo: very-costly
+Certainty: firm
+Record-Id: r-4f2e1a
+Provenance: authored
+CommitLore-Version: 2.0.0
+```
+
+## Standard Trailers
+
+### Ruled-out: [alternative] | [reason]
+
+Decisions explicitly rejected.
+
+```
+Ruled-out: MongoDB | no ACID transactions
+Ruled-out: Redis as primary store | insufficient durability guarantees
+Ruled-out: GraphQL | REST is simpler for our current API surface
+```
+
+**Usage**: Prevent recurring debates about dead options.
+
+**Querying**:
+```bash
+commitlore-org search myorg "database" --trailer Ruled-out
+# Shows: "Ruled-out: MongoDB | ...", "Ruled-out: DynamoDB | ..."
+```
+
+### Limit: [constraint]
+
+Boundaries, prerequisites, or costs of this decision.
+
+```
+Limit: requires Node.js 18+ on all servers
+Limit: team must attend Docker training before deployment
+Limit: adds $5k/month to infrastructure costs
+Limit: cannot scale beyond 100k users without re-architecture
+```
+
+**Usage**: Clarify what this decision requires or constrains.
+
+### Warn: [hazard]
+
+Known gotchas, hazards, or watch-outs.
+
+```
+Warn: connection pooling required or server hits max_connections
+Warn: backfill migration must happen in off-peak hours (>2 hours)
+Warn: DNS cutover can cause 10-30 second outages for old clients
+```
+
+**Usage**: Prevent operational surprises when others implement this decision.
+
+### Blast: [scope]
+
+The blast radius or scope of impact. One of:
+
+- `component`: Affects a single component
+- `service`: Affects a single service or team
+- `system`: Affects the whole system
+- `team`: Affects a team but not architecture
+- `org`: Organization-wide change
+
+```
+Blast: system       # Affects everyone
+Blast: service      # One team owns this
+Blast: component    # Isolated to one module
+```
+
+**Usage**: Prioritize what decisions need broad review and sign-off.
+
+### Undo: [cost]
+
+Cost to reverse this decision. One of:
+
+- `cheap`: Can be undone in hours to days
+- `costly`: Takes weeks to unwind
+- `very-costly`: Months of work or significant risk
+
+```
+Undo: cheap         # Swap back to SQLite in a day
+Undo: costly        # Requires full data migration (2 weeks)
+Undo: very-costly   # Architectural foundation, can't easily revert
+```
+
+**Usage**: Guide how much extra scrutiny a decision needs.
+
+**Convention**: Decisions with `Undo: very-costly` and `Blast: system` typically need broader stakeholder review before committing.
+
+### Certainty: [confidence]
+
+Confidence level in this decision. One of:
+
+- `speculative`: Uncertain, experimental
+- `tentative`: Probable, but room for doubt
+- `firm`: Well-established, unlikely to change
+
+```
+Certainty: speculative  # Trying a new framework
+Certainty: tentative    # Probably right, but learning as we go
+Certainty: firm         # Consensus, years of validation
+```
+
+**Usage**: Signal when to expect future re-evaluation.
+
+### Record-Id: [identifier]
+
+Unique, stable identifier for this decision (for linking and referencing).
+
+```
+Record-Id: r-4f2e1a
+Record-Id: auth-001
+Record-Id: 2024-postgres-migration
+```
+
+**Format**: Recommended: `r-{6 hex digits}` or `{topic}-{number}`.
+
+**Usage**: Link to this decision from other systems (GitHub issues, RFCs, docs).
+
+### Provenance: [source]
+
+How this decision was made. One of:
+
+- `authored`: Explicitly written and committed (someone made a deliberate choice)
+- `inferred`: Derived from code/tests (nobody wrote down the decision, but it's evident)
+
+```
+Provenance: authored    # @alice wrote and committed this decision
+Provenance: inferred    # Decision is evident from code, not explicitly recorded
+```
+
+**Usage**: Distinguish explicit decisions (need context) from inferred ones (derive from code).
+
+### CommitLore-Version: [version]
+
+The version of CommitLore format used (for forward compatibility).
+
+```
+CommitLore-Version: 2.0.0
+```
+
+**Usage**: If the format evolves, tools can handle old and new records.
+
+## Custom Trailers
+
+Organizations can add custom trailers:
+
+```
+Team: backend-platform
+Stakeholders: @alice, @bob, @charlie
+Budget-Impact: $50k/year
+Implementation-Time: 3 weeks
+Risk-Level: high
+OKR-Tied-To: platform-reliability-q4
+```
+
+**Convention**: Use PascalCase or lowercase-with-hyphens. Keep values concise.
+
+## Parsing Rules
+
+1. **Trailer Detection**: After first blank line at end of message, lines matching `Key: Value` are trailers
+2. **Multi-line Values**: Continued lines indented with space or tab
+   ```
+   Ruled-out: MongoDB | reasons:
+    - lacks ACID for complex transactions
+    - requires schema migrations for every field change
+   ```
+3. **Empty Values**: Allowed (key: with nothing after colon)
+   ```
+   Warn: 
+   ```
+4. **Key Format**: Alphanumeric and hyphens (`[a-zA-Z0-9-]+`)
+5. **Case-Insensitive Keys**: `ruled-out`, `Ruled-out`, and `RULED-OUT` are equivalent (normalized to title case for display)
+
+## Best Practices
+
+### When to Write a Decision Record
+
+- Major architectural changes (pick a database, language, framework)
+- Operational choices that will recur (deployment strategy, testing approach)
+- Rejected alternatives worth remembering (saves re-debating)
+- Risk/constraint decisions (compliance, performance guarantees)
+
+**Not needed for**: Bug fixes, feature implementations, routine maintenance.
+
+### Trailer Guidelines
+
+**Write for the next person who asks "Why?", not the team today.**
+
+Good:
+```
+Ruled-out: GraphQL | REST is simpler for our current API surface, 
+  GraphQL adds operational complexity (extra middleware, caching 
+  strategy), and we can migrate later if needed.
+```
+
+Bad:
+```
+Ruled-out: GraphQL | not needed right now
+```
+
+**Be specific about trade-offs.**
+
+```
+Undo: very-costly
+  (not just "costly" — clarifies this is deep in the architecture)
+
+Warn: connection pooling must be enabled or server crashes at >100 concurrent users
+  (not just "connection pooling required" — explains why it matters)
+```
+
+### Collaboration
+
+**Commit together, not separately**: If two people contributed to a decision, both should approve before commit (or use `Provenance: inferred` if deriving from discussion).
+
+**Use Record-Id for linking**:
+```
+GitHub Issue: "Track Postgres switch" #1234
+  Implement decision r-4f2e1a
+
+RFC: "Multi-region deployment strategy"
+  Based on decision r-7f3a2b (DB selection)
+```
+
+## Tool Support
+
+### CommitLore CLI
+
+```bash
+# Search by any trailer
+commitlore search "" --by-trailer Blast system
+
+# Export to other tools
+commitlore search "" --json | jq '.[] | .trailers'
+```
+
+### GitHub / Git
+
+Trailers are standard git metadata, viewable anywhere:
+
+```bash
+git show --format=fuller
+git log --format=%B  # show full message including trailers
+```
+
+## FAQ
+
+### Do I have to use all trailers?
+
+No. Use what's useful for your team:
+- Minimum: `Headline + Body + Record-Id`
+- Recommended add: `Ruled-out + Blast + Undo`
+- Full toolkit: All standard trailers
+
+### Can we define org-wide trailer rules?
+
+Yes, document them in your repo:
+
+```markdown
+# Decision Record Policy
+
+Every architecture decision must include:
+- Clear headline
+- Body explaining why (not just what)
+- Ruled-out section (alternatives considered)
+- Blast scope (system/service/component)
+- Undo cost estimate
+- Record-Id for linking
+
+Optional:
+- Limit (prerequisites, costs)
+- Warn (gotchas)
+- Stakeholders (custom trailer)
+- Budget-Impact (custom trailer)
+```
+
+### What if we change our mind later?
+
+Create a new decision record:
+
+```
+Revisit decision r-4f2e1a: Postgres to CockroachDB
+
+Original: Switch from SQLite to Postgres (r-4f2e1a)
+Now: Scale issues at 500k users, need geo-distribution
+
+Ruled-out: more Postgres replicas | sync latency too high
+Ruled-out: sharding Postgres | operational complexity, connection overhead
+
+Relates-To: r-4f2e1a
+```
+
+### How do we handle sensitive decisions?
+
+CommitLore records are in git history, which is typically shared. For sensitive decisions:
+- Store in a private repository
+- Use `.git/hooks/pre-commit` to validate sensitivity
+- Consider signing with GPG
+- Use `Provenance: redacted` for decisions that can't be shared
+
+## See Also
+
+- [RFC 3797: Requirement Levels](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3797)
+- [Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)](https://adr.github.io/)
+- [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) (for version consistency)

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+
+import fetch from 'node-fetch';
+import { Command } from 'commander';
+import express from 'express';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';
+import { dirname, join } from 'path';
+
+const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
+
+// Parse commit trailers from message
+function parseTrailers(message) {
+  const lines = message.split('\n');
+  const trailers = [];
+
+  let trailerStart = -1;
+  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
+    const line = lines[i].trim();
+    if (!line) {
+      trailerStart = i + 1;
+      break;
+    }
+    if (line.match(/^[\w-]+:/)) {
+      trailerStart = i;
+    } else if (trailerStart > 0) {
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (trailerStart > 0) {
+    for (let i = trailerStart; i < lines.length; i++) {
+      const line = lines[i].trim();
+      if (!line) continue;
+      const match = line.match(/^([\w-]+):\s*(.*)$/);
+      if (match) {
+        trailers.push({ key: match[1], value: match[2] });
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  return trailers;
+}
+
+// Parse commit message into headline, body, trailers
+function parseCommit(message, sha, repository) {
+  const lines = message.split('\n');
+  const headline = lines[0];
+
+  let bodyEnd = lines.length;
+  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
+    if (lines[i].trim().match(/^[\w-]+:/)) {
+      bodyEnd = i;
+    } else if (lines[i].trim() === '' && bodyEnd < lines.length) {
+      bodyEnd = i;
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  const body = lines.slice(1, bodyEnd).join('\n').trim();
+  const trailers = parseTrailers(message);
+
+  return { sha, headline, body, trailers, repository };
+}
+
+// In-memory index for searching
+class OrgIndex {
+  constructor(commits) {
+    this.commits = commits;
+  }
+
+  search(query) {
+    const queryLower = query.toLowerCase();
+    const results = [];
+
+    for (const commit of this.commits) {
+      const matchedTrailers = [];
+      let matches = false;
+
+      for (const trailer of commit.trailers) {
+        const trailerStr = `${trailer.key}: ${trailer.value}`;
+        if (trailerStr.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower)) {
+          matchedTrailers.push(trailerStr);
+          matches = true;
+        }
+      }
+
+      if (!matches && (commit.headline.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower) ||
+          commit.body.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower))) {
+        matches = true;
+      }
+
+      if (matches) {
+        results.push({
+          repository: commit.repository,
+          sha: commit.sha,
+          headline: commit.headline,
+          body: commit.body,
+          trailers: commit.trailers,
+          matchedTrailers
+        });
+      }
+    }
+
+    return results;
+  }
+
+  searchByTrailer(key, value) {
+    const keyLower = key.toLowerCase();
+    const valueLower = value?.toLowerCase();
+    const results = [];
+
+    for (const commit of this.commits) {
+      const matchedTrailers = [];
+
+      for (const trailer of commit.trailers) {
+        if (trailer.key.toLowerCase() === keyLower) {
+          if (!valueLower || trailer.value.toLowerCase().includes(valueLower)) {
+            matchedTrailers.push(`${trailer.key}: ${trailer.value}`);
+          }
+        }
+      }
+
+      if (matchedTrailers.length > 0) {
+        results.push({
+          repository: commit.repository,
+          sha: commit.sha,
+          headline: commit.headline,
+          body: commit.body,
+          trailers: commit.trailers,
+          matchedTrailers
+        });
+      }
+    }
+
+    return results;
+  }
+
+  getStats() {
+    const repos = new Set(this.commits.map(c => c.repository));
+    const trailerTypes = new Set();
+
+    for (const commit of this.commits) {
+      for (const trailer of commit.trailers) {
+        trailerTypes.add(trailer.key);
+      }
+    }
+
+    return {
+      totalCommits: this.commits.length,
+      repositories: repos.size,
+      trailerTypes: Array.from(trailerTypes).sort()
+    };
+  }
+}
+
+// Fetch commits from GitHub GraphQL
+async function fetchCommitsFromGithub({ org, repos, token }) {
+  const query = `
+    query($org: String!, $repos: [String!]) {
+      organization(login: $org) {
+        repositories(first: 100, names: $repos) {
+          nodes {
+            nameWithOwner
+            defaultBranchRef {
+              target {
+                ... on Commit {
+                  history(first: 100) {
+                    edges {
+                      node {
+                        oid
+                        messageHeadline
+                        message
+                      }
+                    }
+                  }
+                }
+              }
+            }
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  `;
+
+  const response = await fetch('https://api.github.com/graphql', {
+    method: 'POST',
+    headers: {
+      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
+      'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`
+    },
+    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables: { org, repos: repos || [] } })
+  });
+
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.statusText}`);
+  }
+
+  const data = await response.json();
+
+  if (data.errors) {
+    throw new Error(`GraphQL error: ${data.errors[0].message}`);
+  }
+
+  const commits = [];
+  for (const repo of data.data.organization.repositories.nodes || []) {
+    if (!repo.defaultBranchRef) continue;
+
+    const edges = repo.defaultBranchRef.target.history.edges || [];
+    for (const edge of edges) {
+      commits.push({
+        ...edge.node,
+        repository: { nameWithOwner: repo.nameWithOwner }
+      });
+    }
+  }
+
+  return commits;
+}
+
+async function buildIndex(org, repos) {
+  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;
+  if (!token) {
+    throw new Error('GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable required. Get one at https://github.com/settings/tokens');
+  }
+
+  console.error(`Fetching commits from GitHub org: ${org}...`);
+  const commits = await fetchCommitsFromGithub({ org, repos, token });
+
+  console.error(`Fetched ${commits.length} commits. Building index from trailers...`);

+  const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;
+  if (!token) {
+    throw new Error(

+    );
+  }
+
+  console.error(`Fetching commits from GitHub org: ${org}...`);

+    org,
+    repos,
+    token,
+  });
+
+  console.error(

+  );
+  const parsed = commits.map((c) =>
+    parseCommit(c.message, c.oid, c.repository.nameWithOwner)

+  const index = new OrgIndex(parsed);
+  return index;

+      );

+      );
+
+      let results;
+      if (options.trailer) {
+        results = index.searchByTrailer(options.trailer, query);
+      } else {
+        results = index.search(query);
+      }

@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
+export interface GithubCommit {
+  oid: string;
+  messageHeadline: string;
+  message: string;
+  repository: {
+    nameWithOwner: string;
+  };
+}
+
+export interface QueryOptions {
+  org: string;
+  repos?: string[];
+  token: string;
+}
+
+const graphqlQuery = `
+  query($org: String!, $repos: [String!]!) {
+    organization(login: $org) {
+      repositories(first: 100, names: $repos) {
+        nodes {
+          nameWithOwner
+          defaultBranchRef {
+            target {
+              ... on Commit {
+                history(first: 100) {
+                  edges {
+                    node {
+                      oid
+                      messageHeadline
+                      message
+                    }
+                  }
+                }
+              }
+            }
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+`;
+
+export async function fetchCommitsFromGithub(
+  options: QueryOptions
+): Promise<GithubCommit[]> {
+  const { org, repos, token } = options;
+
+  const response = await fetch("https://api.github.com/graphql", {
+    method: "POST",
+    headers: {
+      "Content-Type": "application/json",
+      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
+    },
+    body: JSON.stringify({
+      query: graphqlQuery,
+      variables: {
+        org,
+        repos: repos || [],
+      },
+    }),
+  });
+
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.statusText}`);
+  }
+
+  const data: any = await response.json();
+
+  if (data.errors) {
+    throw new Error(`GraphQL error: ${data.errors[0].message}`);
+  }
+
+  const commits: GithubCommit[] = [];
+
+  for (const repo of data.data.organization.repositories.nodes || []) {
+    if (!repo.defaultBranchRef) continue;
+
+    const edges = repo.defaultBranchRef.target.history.edges || [];
+    for (const edge of edges) {
+      commits.push({
+        ...edge.node,
+        repository: { nameWithOwner: repo.nameWithOwner },
+      });
+    }
+  }
+
+  return commits;
+}

+import { ParsedCommit } from "./trailer-parser.js";
+
+export interface SearchResult {
+  repository: string;
+  sha: string;
+  headline: string;
+  body: string;
+  trailers: Array<{ key: string; value: string }>;
+  matchedTrailers: string[];
+}
+
+export class OrgIndex {
+  private commits: ParsedCommit[] = [];
+
+  constructor(commits: ParsedCommit[]) {
+    this.commits = commits;
+  }
+
+  search(query: string): SearchResult[] {
+    const queryLower = query.toLowerCase();
+    const results: SearchResult[] = [];
+
+    for (const commit of this.commits) {
+      const matchedTrailers: string[] = [];
+      let matches = false;
+
+      // Search in trailers
+      for (const trailer of commit.trailers) {
+        const trailerStr = `${trailer.key}: ${trailer.value}`;
+        if (trailerStr.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower)) {
+          matchedTrailers.push(trailerStr);
+          matches = true;
+        }
+      }
+
+      // Search in body and headline
+      if (
+        !matches &&
+        (commit.headline.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower) ||
+          commit.body.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower))
+      ) {
+        matches = true;
+      }
+
+      if (matches) {
+        results.push({
+          repository: commit.repository,
+          sha: commit.sha,
+          headline: commit.headline,
+          body: commit.body,
+          trailers: commit.trailers,
+          matchedTrailers,
+        });
+      }
+    }
+
+    return results;
+  }
+
+  searchByTrailer(key: string, value?: string): SearchResult[] {
+    const keyLower = key.toLowerCase();
+    const valueLower = value?.toLowerCase();
+    const results: SearchResult[] = [];
+
+    for (const commit of this.commits) {
+      const matchedTrailers: string[] = [];
+
+      for (const trailer of commit.trailers) {
+        if (trailer.key.toLowerCase() === keyLower) {
+          if (!valueLower || trailer.value.toLowerCase().includes(valueLower)) {
+            matchedTrailers.push(`${trailer.key}: ${trailer.value}`);
+          }
+        }
+      }
+
+      if (matchedTrailers.length > 0) {
+        results.push({
+          repository: commit.repository,
+          sha: commit.sha,
+          headline: commit.headline,
+          body: commit.body,
+          trailers: commit.trailers,
+          matchedTrailers,
+        });
+      }
+    }
+
+    return results;
+  }
+
+  getStats() {
+    const repoCount = new Set(this.commits.map((c) => c.repository)).size;
+    const trailerTypes = new Set<string>();
+
+    for (const commit of this.commits) {
+      for (const trailer of commit.trailers) {
+        trailerTypes.add(trailer.key);
+      }
+    }
+
+    return {
+      totalCommits: this.commits.length,
+      repositories: repoCount,
+      trailerTypes: Array.from(trailerTypes).sort(),
+    };
+  }
+}

+export interface Trailer {
+  key: string;
+  value: string;
+}
+
+export interface ParsedCommit {
+  sha: string;
+  headline: string;
+  body: string;
+  trailers: Trailer[];
+  repository: string;
+}
+
+function parseTrailers(text: string): Trailer[] {
+  // Git trailers are at the end of commit messages, after blank line
+  // Format: Key: Value
+  const lines = text.split("\n");
+  const trailers: Trailer[] = [];
+
+  // Find where trailers start (usually after blank line at end)
+  let trailerStart = -1;
+  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
+    const line = lines[i].trim();
+    if (!line) {
+      trailerStart = i + 1;
+      break;
+    }
+    // Check if line looks like a trailer (Key: Value)
+    if (line.match(/^[\w-]+:/)) {
+      trailerStart = i;
+    } else if (trailerStart > 0) {
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (trailerStart > 0) {
+    for (let i = trailerStart; i < lines.length; i++) {
+      const line = lines[i].trim();
+      if (!line) continue;
+      const match = line.match(/^([\w-]+):\s*(.*)$/);
+      if (match) {
+        trailers.push({
+          key: match[1],
+          value: match[2],
+        });
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  return trailers;
+}
+
+export function parseCommit(
+  message: string,
+  sha: string,
+  repository: string
+): ParsedCommit {
+  const lines = message.split("\n");
+  const headline = lines[0];
+
+  // Find body end (where trailers start)
+  let bodyEnd = lines.length;
+  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
+    if (lines[i].trim().match(/^[\w-]+:/)) {
+      bodyEnd = i;
+    } else if (lines[i].trim() === "" && bodyEnd < lines.length) {
+      bodyEnd = i;
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  const body = lines.slice(1, bodyEnd).join("\n").trim();
+  const trailers = parseTrailers(message);
+
+  return {
+    sha,
+    headline,
+    body,
+    trailers,
+    repository,
+  };
+}
